evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/users.rs:45-47 register the PUBLIC UNAUTHENTICATED auth endpoints POST /api/v1/users/login (:204 login), POST /api/v1/users/register (:145) and POST /api/v1/users/password-reset (:437) — none of their handler signatures take an auth extractor, and none consult any per-IP / per-account throttle, failed-attempt counter, lockout, backoff or captcha.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/users/mod.rs:251-269 login() does a plain find_user_by_email + verify_password with NO failed-attempt tracking and NO lockout — an attacker can submit unlimited password guesses per account. A crate-wide grep for RateLimit/Governor/tower_governor/throttle/captcha/login_attempt/lockout finds ZERO middleware or handler-level protection (matches are only the unrelated InquiryResult::RateLimited enum variant at handlers/inquiries/mod.rs:36, the observability ErrorCategory::RateLimit label, and saved-search alert daily/weekly throttles). reality-server is internet-facing, so this is an unauthenticated credential-stuffing / password brute-force surface; the same gap makes register an account-spam vector and password-reset a mail/DB-flooding vector.

DISTINCT from the 2026-07-29 'inquiries-no-rate-limit' finding: that covered the anonymous inquiry/viewing spam surface; this is the higher-severity AUTH surface (login brute-force + credential stuffing) on different endpoints. Confidence medium because an upstream gateway/WAF could in principle throttle these, but there is no in-code evidence of it and brute-force protection is normally expected at the app layer. Fix: add per-IP + per-account rate limiting / progressive backoff (or a tower rate-limit layer) in front of login/register/password-reset before the DB lookup.

Multiple internet-facing handlers return the RAW underlying sqlx/anyhow error string as the Axum (StatusCode, String) response body via inline `format!`, bypassing the crate's mandated error boundary crate::util::errors::db_error() (backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/errors.rs:1-33, which documents: 'Reality-server is internet-facing. Raw sqlx::Error / anyhow::Error strings can leak column names, constraint names, sometimes pool / TLS state'). Offenders NOT previously flagged (imports.rs was covered on 2026-07-30): routes/realtors.rs:75,110,154,193,240,273,313; routes/agencies.rs:265,282,319; routes/price_map.rs:153,217; routes/layout.rs:61,67,76,87,96,103; routes/listings.rs:289,301,470.

The bypass is demonstrably inconsistent within the same crate: agent_reviews.rs, compare.rs, favorites.rs and listings.rs' other handlers (:347,:393,:744,:785,:804 return a generic 'Internal server error') already route through db_error() or a static message, proving the intended pattern — the files above simply were not migrated. Fix: replace each inline format!(...e...) map_err arm in realtors.rs / agencies.rs / price_map.rs / layout.rs / listings.rs(cities/search/count) with crate::util::errors::db_error(ctx, e).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/users.rs:453-486 — request_password_reset's success branch (PasswordResetRequestResult::Sent { plaintext_token }) has NO email-delivery step. In debug builds it logs the token (#[cfg(debug_assertions)], :458-463 — correctly gated, not a leak); in release builds (:464-471) it just discards the token (let _ = plaintext_token;) and logs 'Password reset token issued' — the plaintext reset token is NEVER delivered. Inline comment at :455-457 admits it: 'Email transport hasn't been wired yet for the reality server.'

Net effect: the shipped POST /api/v1/users/password-reset always returns 200 'If an account exists for this email, a reset link has been sent.' while in production no reset link is ever sent — account-recovery is silently non-functional for non-SSO password accounts. confirm_password_reset (:501) works, but the token is only obtainable from debug-build logs. Fix: wire an email transport into the Sent branch, or gate/advertise the endpoint as unavailable until transport lands.
